title: WD NAS
description: WD My Cloud OS5 NAS: storage health from WD's own records (the Node Exporter app's wd_ metrics) and the main system metrics

panels.title: Storage health
panels.description: From WD's own records: degraded = e.g. a disk too hot or a RAID rebuilding; critical = a failed disk, a degraded RAID or a volume not mounted

panels.title: RAID

targets.expr: wd_raid_state{instance="$instance"} * on(instance, raid) group_left(level) wd_raid_info{instance="$instance", system="0"}

panels.description: The data RAID's level and state (WD's small system RAID is left out)

panels.title: Hottest disk
panels.description: WD Red drives are rated to 65 °C: orange from 50, red from 58

panels.title: Failed disks

targets.expr: sum(wd_disk_failed{instance="$instance"}) + sum(wd_raid_disks{instance="$instance", state="failed"} * on(instance, raid) group_left wd_raid_info{instance="$instance", system="0"})

panels.description: Disks WD marked as failed, plus failed disks in the data RAID

panels.title: RAID disks
panels.description: The data RAID's disks, by state

targets.expr: wd_raid_disks{instance="$instance"} * on(instance, raid) group_left wd_raid_info{instance="$instance", system="0"}

panels.title: SMART
panels.description: The disks' own SMART health and the attributes that warn of a failing disk: reallocated, pending and uncorrectable sectors (any above 0 deserve attention), and cable / connection errors (CRC). Read every 5 minutes; a sleeping disk isn't woken

panels.title: Problem sectors
panels.description: Each disk's reallocated, pending and uncorrectable sectors together, over time (the SMART table has them separately): rising counts are an early sign of a failing disk

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Reads above the line, writes below
